output.statement: lambda=(ell:Z), ell<p, and dim_C V=n=ell+1. The family (e_i)_{i∈Fin(n)} is a complex basis of V, and y^(ell+1)v=0. One has xe_0=0; xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤ell; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell; ye_ell=0; he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈Fin(n), X_r e_i=choose(ell−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and 0 otherwise; Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤ell and 0 otherwise. All higher y-powers on v vanish after ell.

argument.text: H003 gives lambda≥0, hence lambda=(ell:Z) by the definition of Int.toNat, and ell<p. Thus n=ell+1 and H004 gives dim_C V=n. H006 becomes v≠0, xv=0, hv=ell·v. No property of reduction into K is used here.

produces.statement: lambda=(ell:Z), ell<p, dim_C V=n=ell+1, v≠0, xv=0 and hv=ell·v.

argument.text: H005 gives hy=yh−2y and xy=yx+h. Prove h y^i v=(ell−2i)y^i v for every i≥0 by induction: the base is F001; for the step fix t and temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(ell−2t)y^t v. Then h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(ell−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Discharge L1 to the induction step. For the second identity the base is xyv=yxv+hv=ell v. In the step t≥1, assume L2: xy^t v=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Then xy^(t+1)v=y(xy^t v)+hy^t v=[t(ell−t+1)+(ell−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(ell−t)y^t v. Discharge L2; induction gives xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v for every i≥1. These identities do not assume termination.

produces.statement: For every i≥0, hy^i v=(ell−2i)y^i v; for every i≥1, xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v.

argument.text: For each 0≤i≤ell, repeated use of F002 gives x^i y^i v=[∏_{r=1}^i r(ell−r+1)]v. For i>0 all displayed factors are positive integers; for i=0 the product is 1. In C they are nonzero, so v≠0 forces y^i v≠0. Since i!≠0, e_i≠0. F002 also gives he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. The eigenvalues are pairwise distinct: ell−2i=ell−2j in C implies 2(i−j)=0 and hence i=j in characteristic zero.

produces.statement: For every ii∈Fin(n), e_ii≠0 and he_ii=(ell−2ii)e_ii; the eigenvalue family (ell−2ii)_{ii∈Fin(n)} is pairwise distinct in C.

argument.text: Take arbitrary coefficients zeta and temporarily assume L3: ∑_i zeta_i e_i=0. Fix j∈Fin(n) and apply ∏_{k≠j}(h−(ell−2k)Id). The factors commute because each is a polynomial in h. Every term of index i≠j is killed by its factor k=i; the surviving term is zeta_j[∏_{k≠j}((ell−2j)−(ell−2k))]e_j=0. By F003 the product and e_j are nonzero, including the empty product. Thus zeta_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L3 proves complex linear independence of e.

produces.statement: The family e:Fin(n)→V is C-linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 with division ring C, vector space V, index set Fin(n), and family e. Fin(n) has n elements, V is finite-dimensional of dimension n by F001, and F004 supplies independence. The span is V. Together with independence this makes e a basis.

produces.statement: The family e:Fin(n)→V is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Put zvec=y^(ell+1)v and alpha_i its e-basis coordinates. M006 with this basis expands zvec=∑_i alpha_i e_i. F002 gives h zvec=(−ell−2)zvec, and applying h−(−ell−2)Id to this expansion gives ∑_i alpha_i[2(ell+1−i)]e_i=0. For every i≤ell the bracketed integer is positive, hence nonzero in C. Independence F004 forces every alpha_i=0, so zvec=0. Applying further powers of y gives y^s v=0 for all s≥ell+1.

produces.statement: y^(ell+1)v=0, and y^s v=0 for every natural s≥ell+1.

argument.text: Divide the recurrences F002 by i!, using (i+1)!=(i+1)i!, and combine F006 at the top endpoint. This gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell, ye_ell=0 and he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For r≤i, iteration of x yields ∏_{s=1}^r(ell−i+s) on e_(i−r). After division by r!, M004 at (n0,j0)=(ell−i+r,r), and cancellation of (ell−i)!≠0 in C, gives choose(ell−i+r,r). If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed. For i+r≤ell, iteration of y yields (i+r)!/i! on e_(i+r); division by r!, using M004 at (i+r,r), gives choose(i+r,r). If i+r>ell the string reaches e_ell and is killed by y. Thus both zero cases and r=0 are included. These formulas together with F001,F005,F006 prove the full coordinate and termination statement.

F005 supplies the e-basis and Fin(n) is finite.
zvec is an explicit vector in V, because y is an endomorphism and v∈V.
